openIssues.description: The en record now fingerprints legacyAliases(registry, pageId, "en") = {} instead of the page-level alias map, so an edit to a zh-CN historic alias changes only the zh-CN record. The en HTML nevertheless serializes the zh-CN section inventory, including those aliases, into the language switch data-section-ids attribute (LanguageSwitcher.astro lines 10-15; e.g. dist docs/quickstart/index.html lists 生成-apkg and 继续完成实际任务). Behaviorally inert for en→zh-CN switching (alias targets are already-covered stable ids or _top, and en mappings never yield zh-CN slugs), and consistent with the pre-existing scope in which en records never fingerprinted zh-CN heading slugs either. No current record is affected: all 69 HTML pages are byte-identical to HEAD. Recorded so a later change to that attribute or to cross-locale anchor semantics re-examines it.

legacyAliases validates locale keys against the main checkout's imported configuredLocales, not the supplied review root's locale-model.mjs, unlike the rest of the review projection, which reads literal data from the supplied root. Executed: a disposable root that registers an "it" locale and adds "it" aliases is rejected with "Unknown legacy section locale: it". Fails closed and never yields a wrong hash; it only limits supplied-root fixtures.

The new "releasing a locale is a data change" list omits website/language-briefs.json, which reviewInputs requires for every reviewed locale (content-review-inputs.mjs:206-207 throws "missing or stale language brief"); the content-contract third-locale test adds it explicitly. Documentation completeness only; no effect on any record.
